subject: Bootstrap in SEM  with categorical indicators which are hevily skewed

messages.author: 4d60065baa5c0933
messages.subject: Bootstrap in SEM  with categorical indicators which are hevily skewed
parts:
Hello, 

I'm doing a two-group SEM with two latent variables measured by categorical indicators, one by continuous indicators and binary DVs.
The model in lavaan reports good fit(CFI TLI >.96)
But the reviewer asks for bootstrap indirect effect. So, I did bootstrap analysis in mplus using the same estimator (WLSMV). But the bootstrap result is very different from the no bootstrap result. Many paths became non-significant and some changed direction.

My categorical indicators(2 or 3 levels) are heavily skewed(95%-99% are zero) , is this the reason why this could have happened. 

I have searched through many resources but couldn't find an answer. 
I hope that you can help me solve this problem.

messages.author: 12fdd832cacb825e
messages.subject: Re: Bootstrap in SEM with categorical indicators which are hevily skewed
parts:
Nimo,

Yes, the skew is likely the problem. Unless your sample is massive, you're likely going to get bootstrap draws with no variance in one or more categorical indicators. Either Mplus or bootstrapping in R should tell you that some of the draws did not produce a solution. If that number is substantial, you shouldn't rely on the bootstrap.

The change in sign is also indicative of this. If the percentile bootstrap is working well, its central tendency should be about the same as the original, non-bootstrap estimates.

Pat

messages.subject: Re: Bootstrap in SEM with categorical indicators which are hevily skewed
parts:
Dear Prof. Malone

Thanks for your answer. Indeed, when I use bootstraplavaan to get bootstrap results, it reports"lavaan WARNING: 42 bivariate tables have empty cells in every bootstrap draw. So, can I calculate the CI using the distribution of the product (Za*Zb) method in RMediation? Would this approach better than reporting the estimates of defined parameters in the lavaan model in my case( skewed categorical indicators and continuous indicators + categorical DVs ). 
It seems that defined parameters in lavaan are calculated using a*b(both standardized) and indirect effects in RMediation are calculated using (Za*Zb)'s distribution. Though in my model, they produce very similar results. 

Thanks!
Nimo
